opportunities.title: Regular Grants (operating/core costs, project, and capital)

amount.raw: Regular grants are for grants under £100,000 (grants of £100,000 and over are Major Grants)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charities, Charitable Incorporated Organisations (CIOs), and exempt or excepted organisations per Charity Commission guidelines; must have at least one year's worth of annual accounts (independently audited/examined or Charity Commission annual return); must work inside the UK or UK Overseas Territories; only one application at a time per organisation (one year must pass after a previous decision before re-applying).
opportunities.summary: Rolling grant programme providing funding to UK charities for operating/core costs, specific projects/activities, or capital projects. Grants are reviewed in the order received; decisions typically within 4-6 months. Grantees can use operating/core cost grants towards general running costs including overall salary bills (but not specific posts). Project and capital grants typically 10-20% of total project cost (capital no more than 10%, up to £30,000 for local community projects).

opportunities.title: Major Grants (£100,000 and over)

amount.raw: Major grants are £100,000 and over; the total cost of what is being applied for must be at least £1 million

opportunities.eligibility_summary: For Major Grants the total cost of the application must be at least £1 million. For core costs, the organisation's annual income must be £1 million or over. For capital or project costs, the organisation's income need not exceed £1 million but the total project cost must be at least £1 million. Must be a UK registered charity, CIO, or exempt/excepted organisation and pass the eligibility quiz.
opportunities.summary: Rolling major grant programme for grants of £100,000 and over. Applicants submit a Major Grant Expression of Interest Form via the Grants Management Portal, receive bespoke guidance within 10 working days, and may be invited for a call if potentially suitable. Local community capital projects (e.g. churches, village halls) are advised to apply for a regular grant instead.
